# Data & AI Wiki

> Alex Merced's short-definition wiki for AI and data terms: agents, LLMs, retrieval, semantic layers, lakehouses, and the platforms around them. Each page gives a brief definition of one term. Long-form guides live on DataEngnr (https://dataengnr.com).

## Core Pages

- [Home](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/) - Main entry point and directory list.
- [Terms](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/terms/) - Complete list of Data & AI terms.
- [Individuals](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/individuals/) - Key individuals in the Data & AI space.
- [Vendor Platforms](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/vendor-platforms/) - Overview of vendor platforms.

## Wiki Articles

- [ACID](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/acid/) - ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability, the properties that keep database transactions reliable through crashes and power failures.
- [Active Learning](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/active-learning/) - A semi-supervised machine learning paradigm where the algorithm selects which unlabeled data points it needs labeled next to improve training efficiency.
- [Ad-hoc Query](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/ad-hoc-query/) - An ad-hoc query is written on demand to answer a one-time business question rather than run on a schedule. Analysts lean on them for BI and data exploration.
- [Agentic AI](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/agentic-ai/) - In agentic AI, models act as autonomous agents that plan, use tools, run complex workflows, and make decisions toward a goal without step-by-step human help.
- [Aggregation](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/aggregation/) - Aggregation groups many data values into one summary value such as a sum, average, or count. It is the basic operation behind most reports and KPI metrics.
- [AI-ism](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/ai-ism/) - An AI-ism is a cliched, repetitive, or sterile phrase typical of generic AI-generated text. Editorial best practice says to cut such phrases from final copy.
- [Airflow](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/airflow/) - Apache Airflow is an open-source platform for authoring, scheduling, and monitoring workflows in code, with each pipeline defined as a DAG of dependent tasks.
- [Alex Merced](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/alex-merced/) - Alex Merced is Head of Developer Relations at Dremio and an author and speaker on data lakehouses, Apache Iceberg, and Apache Polaris, with 77 books written.
- [Analytics Engineer](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/analytics-engineer/) - Analytics engineers sit between data engineering and analysis, writing modular, tested SQL and dbt code that turns raw data into well-modeled tables for BI.
- [ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/ann-approximate-nearest-neighbor/) - Approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search finds vectors close to a query vector, giving up a little accuracy for large speed gains in big similarity searches.
- [Anomaly Detection](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/anomaly-detection/) - Anomaly detection is the identification of rare items, events, or observations that raise suspicion because they differ sharply from the majority of the data.
- [Apache Hudi](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/apache-hudi/) - Apache Hudi is an open-source lakehouse table format that brings upserts, deletes, and incremental processing pipelines to data sitting in cloud object storage.
- [Apache Iceberg](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/apache-iceberg/) - Apache Iceberg is an open table format for huge analytic datasets. It lets Spark, Trino, Flink, and Dremio safely share one copy of data using SQL behavior.
- [Apache Polaris](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/apache-polaris/) - Apache Polaris is an open-source lakehouse catalog for Apache Iceberg, offering centralized access control, cross-engine credential vending, and multi-tenancy.
- [Apache Spark](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/apache-spark/) - Apache Spark is an open-source distributed engine for batch, streaming, SQL, and machine learning work. In-memory computation is its edge over Hadoop MapReduce.
- [Apache Spark Structured Streaming](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/apache-spark-structured-streaming/) - A scalable and fault-tolerant stream processing engine built on the Spark SQL engine, allowing streaming queries to be expressed like batch queries.
- [API (Application Programming Interface)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/api-application-programming-interface/) - An API is a set of protocols and tools that lets software applications talk to each other, defining the methods and data formats used to request information.
- [API Gateway](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/api-gateway/) - An API gateway is the single entry point between clients and backend microservices, handling request routing, API composition, rate limits, and authentication.
- [Artificial Intelligence](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/artificial-intelligence/) - Artificial intelligence is the simulation of human intelligence by machines, covering learning from information, reasoning to conclusions, and self-correction.
- [Artificial Neural Network](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/artificial-neural-network/) - A computing system modeled after the human brain's neural structure, containing layers of interconnected nodes used to solve non-linear learning problems.
- [Athena](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/athena/) - Amazon Athena is a serverless query service for analyzing data in Amazon S3 with standard SQL. There is no infrastructure to manage, and you pay per query run.
- [Attention Mechanism](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/attention-mechanism/) - Attention is the Transformer component that lets a model focus on the most relevant parts of an input sequence as it generates output, for long-range context.
- [Autoencoder](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/autoencoder/) - A type of unsupervised artificial neural network used to learn efficient data codings or compressions by training the network to ignore signal noise.
- [Avro](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/avro/) - Apache Avro is a row-oriented serialization system with a compact binary format and schemas written in JSON, a common fit for Kafka event streaming setups.
- [AVX-512](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/avx-512/) - A set of CPU instructions that support advanced vector extensions, frequently utilized to accelerate vector search calculations and machine learning inference.
- [AWS (Amazon Web Services)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/aws-amazon-web-services/) - Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a cloud platform offering more than 200 services from data centers worldwide, including compute power, storage, and databases.
- [AWS Glue](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/aws-glue/) - A serverless data integration service that makes it easy to discover, prepare, and combine data for analytics, machine learning, and application development.
- [Azure (Microsoft Azure)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/azure-microsoft-azure/) - Microsoft Azure is Microsoft's cloud computing platform, offering analytics, virtual machines, database management, and AI services tied into Microsoft systems.
- [Azure Blob Storage](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/azure-blob-storage/) - Azure Blob Storage is Microsoft Azure's object storage service for very large amounts of unstructured text or binary data, often used in cloud-native analytics.
- [Backpropagation](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/backpropagation/) - Backpropagation trains neural networks by computing the loss gradient for each weight and passing errors backward from the output layer to adjust the weights.
- [Bag-of-Words](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/bag-of-words/) - A simple text representation model used in NLP where a text document is represented as an unordered bag or set of its words, ignoring grammar and word order.
- [BASE](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/base/) - BASE stands for Basically Available, Soft state, Eventual consistency. Distributed databases use it to favor availability and scale over the immediacy of ACID.
- [Batch Size](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/batch-size/) - Batch size is a machine learning hyperparameter that sets how many training samples a model processes in one iteration before its parameters are updated.
- [Bfloat16](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/bfloat16/) - Brain Floating Point 16-bit format, a truncated version of the 32-bit float format designed to accelerate machine learning computations and save memory.
- [BI (Business Intelligence)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/bi-business-intelligence/) - A technology-driven process for analyzing data and delivering actionable information to help executives, managers, and workers make informed business decisions.
- [Bias-Variance Tradeoff](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/bias-variance-tradeoff/) - The bias-variance tradeoff is the tension between error from wrong assumptions (bias) and error from sensitivity to noise in training data (variance).
- [BigQuery](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/bigquery/) - BigQuery is Google Cloud's fully managed, serverless enterprise data warehouse. It runs fast SQL queries over petabytes of data on Google's own infrastructure.
- [Blob Storage](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/blob-storage/) - A category of cloud storage optimized for storing unstructured binary large objects (blobs) such as videos, audio, backups, and large analytical datasets.
- [Boosting](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/boosting/) - An ensemble machine learning technique that trains weak learners sequentially, with each new model focusing on correcting the errors of its predecessor.
- [Bootstrap Aggregating (Bagging)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/bootstrap-aggregating-bagging/) - An ensemble machine learning meta-algorithm designed to improve the stability and accuracy of algorithms, reducing variance and avoiding overfitting.
- [Business Glossary](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/business-glossary/) - A centralized directory containing definitions of business terms, concepts, and relationships, separate from physical database table schema catalogs.
- [Cache](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/cache/) - A cache stores data temporarily so later requests for it are served faster. In databases and search engines, caching cuts query latency and lowers server load.
- [Catalog](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/catalog/) - In database systems, a catalog is a metadata repository containing definitions of database objects such as tables, views, columns, and security privileges.
- [CDC (Change Data Capture)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/cdc-change-data-capture/) - Change data capture (CDC) tracks inserts, updates, and deletes in a database as they happen, so downstream systems can react to each change in real time.
- [CDN (Content Delivery Network)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/cdn-content-delivery-network/) - A content delivery network (CDN) is a geographically spread set of servers that cache web assets close to users, cutting page load delays for internet content.
- [Classification](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/classification/) - Classification is a supervised machine learning task where a model assigns each incoming data point to one of a fixed set of discrete classes or labels.
- [ClickHouse](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/clickhouse/) - ClickHouse is an open-source columnar database built for real-time analytics. It uses SQL and is tuned to process petabytes of data with very low latency.
- [Cloud Storage](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/cloud-storage/) - Cloud storage keeps data on the internet with a provider that runs the storage as a managed service, offering scale and durability without owning the hardware.
- [Clustering](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/clustering/) - In databases, clustering organizes table storage by the values of one or more columns so related rows sit physically together and range queries run faster.
- [Clustering Algorithm](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/clustering-algorithm/) - A clustering algorithm is an unsupervised learning method that groups data points by a similarity metric. K-Means and DBSCAN are two examples of the type.
- [Colocation](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/colocation/) - Colocation means placing compute, data engines, or storage resources in the same data center so that network latency between them stays as low as possible.
- [Columnar Database](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/columnar-database/) - A columnar database stores tables by column rather than by row. For analytical (OLAP) queries this layout cuts disk I/O and compresses data more effectively.
- [Compaction](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/compaction/) - Compaction reorganizes storage files in transactional data lakes and databases, merging many small files into fewer large ones and resolving deletes.
- [Compaction Job](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/compaction-job/) - A compaction job is a scheduled worker process that rewrites the transactional log files behind a table so that queries against it execute faster.
- [Compute-Storage Separation](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/compute-storage-separation/) - Compute-storage separation lets a data platform scale and pay for storage and query engines independently, which avoids resource contention and lowers costs.
- [Computer Cluster](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/computer-cluster/) - A set of loosely or tightly connected computers that work together as a single system, essential for executing distributed query engines like Spark or Trino.
- [Computer Vision](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/computer-vision/) - Computer vision is the field of AI that trains machines to interpret the visual world. Deep learning models use digital images to identify and classify objects.
- [Consensus Protocol](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/consensus-protocol/) - A consensus protocol lets multiple unreliable nodes in a distributed system agree on one data value or system state, giving reliability and fault tolerance.
- [Containerization](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/containerization/) - A lightweight virtualization method that packages an application and its dependencies into a single container image, executed uniformly across environments.
- [Context Window](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/context-window/) - The context window is the most tokens a large language model can handle in one prompt and response. A larger window lets the model reference longer documents.
- [Copy-on-Write](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/copy-on-write/) - Copy-on-write never edits data files in place. Each write copies the original data, applies the change, and writes a new file, keeping transactions isolated.
- [Correlation](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/correlation/) - A statistical relationship indicating how closely two variables fluctuate together, ranging from perfect positive correlation to perfect negative correlation.
- [Cosine Similarity](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/cosine-similarity/) - Cosine similarity scores how alike two vectors are from the cosine of the angle between them. It is a standard measure in document similarity and vector search.
- [Cross-Validation](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/cross-validation/) - A resampling method used to evaluate machine learning models by partitioning data into training and validation folds to obtain stable metrics.
- [DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/dag-directed-acyclic-graph/) - A directed acyclic graph (DAG) maps tasks and their dependencies as edges with no loops, so a workflow can run in a reliable, ordered sequence of steps.
- [Dagster](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/dagster/) - Dagster is a cloud-native orchestrator for machine learning, analytics, and ETL that treats data assets as first-class objects and stresses local testing.
- [Dashboard](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/dashboard/) - A dashboard is a visual interface showing KPIs, metrics, and analytical data points that summarize how an organization or process is performing at a glance.
- [Data Analyst](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-analyst/) - A data analyst collects, cleans, and statistically analyzes data to support business decisions, then shares results through reports and dashboards.
- [Data Asset](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-asset/) - A data asset is any structured or unstructured file, table, database, or dashboard that holds business value and is managed within an organization.
- [Data Catalog](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-catalog/) - A data catalog is a metadata-driven inventory of an organization's data assets that helps data teams find, evaluate, and manage the datasets they need.
- [Data Cube](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-cube/) - A data cube is a multi-dimensional view of data used in business intelligence, letting users analyze the same figures by time, geography, or product line.
- [Data Democratization](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-democratization/) - The process of making data accessible to non-technical users within an organization without requiring specialized assistance from IT or data engineering teams.
- [Data Engineer](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-engineer/) - Data engineers design, build, test, and maintain the pipelines, warehouses, and architectures that keep data clean, reliable, and ready for analytics.
- [Data Fabric](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-fabric/) - A data fabric connects and manages data across systems, clouds, and physical locations, relying on metadata to automate integration and access control.
- [Data Federation](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-federation/) - Data federation lets users query several separate data sources as if they were one database, without copying or physically moving any of the underlying data.
- [Data Governance](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-governance/) - Data governance is the set of practices and processes for formally managing an organization's data assets, covering security, privacy, compliance, and catalogs.
- [Data Ingestion](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-ingestion/) - The process of importing, loading, and transferring raw data from external source systems into a data warehouse or data lakehouse storage repository.
- [Data Lake](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-lake/) - A data lake is a central repository for structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data at any scale, typically built on top of cloud object storage.
- [Data Lakehouse](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-lakehouse/) - A data lakehouse pairs the cheap, scalable object storage of a data lake with the ACID transactions and SQL performance of a data warehouse in one architecture.
- [Data Lakehouse Catalog](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-lakehouse-catalog/) - A data lakehouse catalog is the software interface that tracks transaction log structures, namespaces, and metadata file locations across a lakehouse.
- [Data Lineage](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-lineage/) - Data lineage traces data from its origin through each transformation to its final destination across systems and pipelines, aiding debugging and governance.
- [Data Lineage Graph](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-lineage-graph/) - A data lineage graph is a visual map showing where data columns originate, which transformation steps they pass through, and where they end up.
- [Data Marketplace](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-marketplace/) - A data marketplace is an online platform where organizations publish, sell, license, or buy standardized datasets and analytical products from other parties.
- [Data Mart](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-mart/) - A subset of a data warehouse focused on a single functional area, department, or subject, designed to provide data quickly to a specific group of users.
- [Data Mesh](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-mesh/) - Data mesh is a decentralized architecture that organizes data by business domain instead of central pipelines, treating data as a product owned by domain teams.
- [Data Modeling](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-modeling/) - Data modeling defines the structure, relationships, constraints, and formats of a database or warehouse so storage stays consistent and queries run well.
- [Data Pipeline](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-pipeline/) - A series of automated data processing steps that moves data from a source system to a destination system, transforming and cleaning it along the way.
- [Data Quality](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-quality/) - Data quality is the measure of how accurate, complete, reliable, and relevant data is for business operations and for analytical decision-making.
- [Data Refresh](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-refresh/) - A data refresh is the scheduled update of data warehouses, data marts, or dashboards with the latest records pulled from transactional source systems.
- [Data Retention](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-retention/) - Data retention covers the policies and technical settings that decide how long records and tables are kept in storage before they are deleted or archived.
- [Data Science](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-science/) - An interdisciplinary field combining statistics, programming, and domain expertise to extract insights and build predictive models from data.
- [Data Scientist](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-scientist/) - A data scientist applies statistics, machine learning, and predictive modeling to solve complex business problems and uncover insights hidden in data.
- [Data Sharing](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-sharing/) - Data sharing gives external partners or other departments secure access to database tables or lakehouse datasets without copying the underlying files to them.
- [Data Silo](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-silo/) - A data silo is an isolated pocket of data inside an organization that one department can reach while the rest of the company is cut off from it.
- [Data Source](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-source/) - A data source is where data originates, such as a transactional database, application API, log file, or IoT sensor, before analytical engines import it.
- [Data Sovereignty](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-sovereignty/) - Data sovereignty is the principle that digital data falls under the laws and governance structures of the country where that data is physically located.
- [Data Steward](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-steward/) - A data steward maintains the quality, metadata, and security policies of datasets, acting as the accountable custodian for the data assets in their care.
- [Data Stewardship](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-stewardship/) - Data stewardship is the operational responsibility for managing data assets: keeping quality high, cataloging metadata, and ensuring policy compliance.
- [Data Transformation](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-transformation/) - Data transformation is the process of cleaning, converting, and formatting raw data into structured tables that are optimized for reporting and analysis.
- [Data Virtualization](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-virtualization/) - Data virtualization lets applications retrieve and manipulate data without knowing technical details such as its format or where it physically lives.
- [Data Warehouse](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/data-warehouse/) - A data warehouse is a centralized, highly structured repository built for business intelligence, analytical queries, and reporting across historical datasets.
- [Database Index](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/database-index/) - A database index is a structured pointer table built on columns so value filters run faster. The tradeoff is the extra disk space the index consumes.
- [Databricks](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/databricks/) - Databricks is a cloud data platform built on Apache Spark, Delta Lake, and MLflow, serving data engineering, collaborative data science, and business analytics.
- [DBT (Data Build Tool)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/dbt-data-build-tool/) - dbt (data build tool) is an open-source command-line tool for transforming warehouse data with SQL select statements, with version control and testing built in.
- [Decoder](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/decoder/) - A decoder is the part of a sequence-to-sequence model like a Transformer that turns encoded representations into output token by token, as in text generation.
- [Deep Learning](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/deep-learning/) - Deep learning is the branch of machine learning built on neural networks with many layers. It tackles hard problems in vision, language, and prediction tasks.
- [Deep Neural Network](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/deep-neural-network/) - A deep neural network has multiple hidden layers between its input and output layers, and those stacked layers let it learn high-level features from data.
- [Delta Lake](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/delta-lake/) - Delta Lake is an open-source table format created by Databricks that adds ACID transactions, scalable metadata, and unified streaming and batch to data lakes.
- [Denormalization](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/denormalization/) - Denormalization deliberately adds redundant data to a schema to speed up queries. Fewer complex table joins are needed when related values are stored together.
- [Differentiable Programming](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/differentiable-programming/) - A programming paradigm where programs can be differentiated, allowing parameters to be optimized using gradient descent, common in deep learning.
- [Dimension Table](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/dimension-table/) - A dimension table holds descriptive attributes in a star schema, such as customer name or product category, used to filter and group metrics in fact tables.
- [Dimensional Modeling](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/dimensional-modeling/) - A database design technique optimized for analytical queries, organizing data into star or snowflake schemas containing fact and dimension tables.
- [Distributed Database](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/distributed-database/) - A distributed database spreads its files across two or more physical sites, on one network or several, and is designed to scale out horizontally as data grows.
- [Distributed Query](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/distributed-query/) - A distributed query is one that runs in parallel across multiple database instances or cluster computing nodes, with each node handling part of the work.
- [Docker](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/docker/) - Docker is an open-source platform that deploys applications in lightweight, portable containers so they behave the same in development, testing, and production.
- [Document Store](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/document-store/) - A type of NoSQL database designed to store, retrieve, and manage semi-structured data as document objects, typically formatted in JSON or XML (e.g., MongoDB).
- [Dot Product](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/dot-product/) - The dot product takes two equal-length sequences of numbers, usually vectors, and returns one number. Vector databases use it to measure vector alignment.
- [Double-bracket link](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/double-bracket-link/) - A double-bracket link is wiki-style syntax for linking to another page by its title. On this site those links become relative paths at build time.
- [Dremio](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/dremio/) - Dremio is an open SQL lakehouse engine that queries data in place on S3, ADLS, and GCS object storage, using an Apache Arrow engine and a semantic layer.
- [DuckDB](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/duckdb/) - DuckDB is an open-source, embedded columnar database for analytical queries. Often called the SQLite for analytics, it runs in the host process with no server.
- [ELT (Extract, Load, Transform)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/elt-extract-load-transform/) - ELT (extract, load, transform) loads raw source data straight into a target such as a data warehouse, then transforms it there using the target's compute.
- [Embedding](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/embedding/) - An embedding represents words, documents, or images as dense numerical vectors in a high-dimensional space that captures their meaning and relationships.
- [Embedding Layer](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/embedding-layer/) - An embedding layer is the neural network layer that maps discrete tokens or categorical features to dense, low-dimensional vector representations.
- [Embedding Model](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/embedding-model/) - An embedding model is a machine learning model trained to turn text, images, and other inputs into vector embeddings that preserve semantic relationships.
- [Encoder](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/encoder/) - An encoder is the part of a neural network, such as a Transformer, that turns input data into a contextual vector representation a decoder can then interpret.
- [Entity Resolution](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/entity-resolution/) - Entity resolution identifies and links records across separate datasets that refer to the same real-world entity, such as one customer stored under several IDs.
- [Epoch](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/epoch/) - An epoch is one complete pass of the entire training dataset through a machine learning model's training algorithm, from the first sample to the last.
- [ETL (Extract, Transform, Load)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/etl-extract-transform-load/) - ETL (extract, transform, load) pulls data from source systems, cleans and transforms it on a staging server, then loads the result into a data warehouse.
- [ETL Metadata](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/etl-metadata/) - Data about data generated during integration processes, detailing pipeline execution times, raw row counts, transformed column schemas, and pipeline status.
- [Euclidean Distance](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/euclidean-distance/) - The straight-line distance between two points in Euclidean space. In vector search, it is used to measure the dissimilarity between two vector representations.
- [Event-driven Architecture](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/event-driven-architecture/) - A software architecture pattern where decoupled services react to events generated by other parts of the system in real-time, often using brokers like Kafka.
- [Execution Plan](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/execution-plan/) - An execution plan is the sequence of operations a query optimizer chooses to read or update data, listing indexes used, join algorithms, and execution costs.
- [Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/exploratory-data-analysis-eda/) - Exploratory data analysis (EDA) summarizes a dataset's main statistical characteristics, often with plots and other visuals, before any formal modeling begins.
- [F1 Score](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/f1-score/) - The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, folding both into one number that measures the accuracy of a binary classification model.
- [Fact Table](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/fact-table/) - A fact table sits at the center of a star schema, storing quantitative measurements (facts) alongside foreign keys that reference dimension tables.
- [False Negative](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/false-negative/) - A false negative is a classification error where the model predicts the negative class for a data point that actually belongs to the positive class.
- [False Positive](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/false-positive/) - A false positive is a classification error where the model predicts the positive class for a data point that actually belongs to the negative class.
- [Feature Engineering](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/feature-engineering/) - Feature engineering selects, manipulates, and transforms raw data into new, informative features that improve a machine learning model's predictions.
- [Feature Selection](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/feature-selection/) - Feature selection is the preprocessing step of choosing the most informative variables to train a machine learning algorithm, leaving the rest out.
- [Feature Store](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/feature-store/) - A feature store is a central repository for storing and serving curated machine learning features, keeping offline training and online inference consistent.
- [Feature Vector](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/feature-vector/) - A feature vector is an n-dimensional list of numerical features that describes one object. Machine learning models take feature vectors as their standard input.
- [Federated Query Engine](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/federated-query-engine/) - A federated query engine such as Trino is a distributed SQL processor that runs one query across several external databases at once without copying their data.
- [Few-Shot Learning](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/few-shot-learning/) - Few-shot learning is a machine learning scenario in which a model is trained or prompted to perform a task using only a small number of examples.
- [Fine-tuning](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/fine-tuning/) - Fine-tuning takes a pre-trained machine learning model and trains it further on a smaller, task-specific dataset to adapt its abilities to a specialized domain.
- [Fivetran](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/fivetran/) - Fivetran is a managed ELT platform that loads data from SaaS apps, databases, and file stores into warehouses or lakehouses, using log-based CDC for updates.
- [Flink (Apache Flink)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/flink-apache-flink/) - Apache Flink is an open-source distributed stream processing framework for continuous data streams, built for low latency, high throughput, and stateful events.
- [Fully Connected Layer](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/fully-connected-layer/) - A fully connected layer is a neural network layer in which every node links to every node in the preceding layer, so each output depends on all of the inputs.
- [GCP (Google Cloud Platform)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/gcp-google-cloud-platform/) - Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is Google's suite of cloud services for infrastructure, analytics, storage, databases, and ML, on hardware Google uses itself.
- [Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/generative-adversarial-network-gan/) - A generative adversarial network (GAN) pits two neural networks, a generator and a discriminator, against each other to produce realistic synthetic data.
- [Generative AI](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/generative-ai/) - Generative AI is the branch of AI that creates new text, images, code, and music, using models trained on massive datasets of existing human-made content.
- [Glowmorphism](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/glowmorphism/) - Glowmorphism is a visual design style built from neon highlights, glowing borders, and drop shadows over dark translucent backdrops for high-contrast UIs.
- [Google Cloud Storage](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/google-cloud-storage/) - Google Cloud Storage is Google Cloud Platform's object storage service, used for serving website content, holding backups, and storing large analytics files.
- [GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/gpt-generative-pre-trained-transformer/) - GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) names a family of decoder-only transformer language models trained on huge text corpora for many text generation tasks.
- [GPU (Graphics Processing Unit)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/gpu-graphics-processing-unit/) - A GPU (graphics processing unit) is a specialized circuit built for fast memory manipulation, now widely used to speed up model training and heavy vector math.
- [Gradient Descent](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/gradient-descent/) - Gradient descent minimizes a model's loss function by repeatedly nudging its weights in the direction of steepest descent until the error stops falling.
- [Graph Database](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/graph-database/) - A graph database is a NoSQL store that models data as nodes, edges, and properties, built for querying highly connected relationships such as social networks.
- [GraphQL](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/graphql/) - An open-source data query and manipulation language for APIs, allowing clients to request exactly the data they need and nothing more, reducing network usage.
- [Guardrails](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/guardrails/) - Guardrails are safety filters on generative AI systems that block harmful inputs and toxic outputs, enforce policy compliance, and help reduce hallucinations.
- [Hallucination](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/hallucination/) - A phenomenon where a Generative AI model or Large Language Model generates output that is factually incorrect, nonsensical, or unaligned with its training data.
- [Heuristic](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/heuristic/) - A heuristic is a practical rule of thumb for solving problems quickly rather than exhaustively. Query optimizers use them to draft initial query paths.
- [Hidden Partitioning](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/hidden-partitioning/) - Hidden partitioning is an Apache Iceberg feature that derives partition values from source columns, so queries get pruning without naming partition filters.
- [Hive Metastore](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/hive-metastore/) - The Hive Metastore is the traditional central metadata catalog of the Apache Hadoop ecosystem, storing table schemas and the directory paths of table data.
- [HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/hnsw-hierarchical-navigable-small-world/) - HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is a graph-based approximate nearest neighbor algorithm using multi-layer graphs for fast high-dimensional search.
- [Hot Tier](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/hot-tier/) - A hot tier is a high-performance storage tier for active data that is queried frequently. It is served from fast SSDs or in-memory caches to speed up access.
- [Hudi Timeline](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/hudi-timeline/) - A core log structure in Apache Hudi that tracks all actions performed on a table, providing transactional guarantees and point-in-time queries.
- [Hyperparameter](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/hyperparameter/) - A hyperparameter is a machine learning setting fixed before training starts, such as learning rate or batch size, that governs how the model learns from data.
- [IaC (Infrastructure as Code)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/iac-infrastructure-as-code/) - Infrastructure as code (IaC) provisions and manages servers, databases, and networks through machine-readable config files instead of manual, interactive tools.
- [IAM (Identity and Access Management)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/iam-identity-and-access-management/) - Identity and access management (IAM) is the set of policies and tools ensuring the right people and systems get the right access to cloud resources.
- [Iceberg Manifest](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/iceberg-manifest/) - An Iceberg manifest is an Avro file in an Apache Iceberg table that lists individual data files and records file-level statistical bounds used for pruning.
- [Iceberg REST Catalog](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/iceberg-rest-catalog/) - The Iceberg REST Catalog is a standard REST API spec for managing Apache Iceberg tables, so query engines can safely exchange metadata with one catalog.
- [In-database Analytics](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/in-database-analytics/) - In-database analytics runs analytical algorithms and machine learning models inside the database engine itself, avoiding the delays of exporting data.
- [In-memory Database](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/in-memory-database/) - An in-memory database keeps its data mainly in RAM instead of on disk, which makes reads and writes far faster than in a disk-bound database management system.
- [Incremental Load](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/incremental-load/) - An incremental load is an ETL or ELT process that updates a target database with only the records new or changed since the last run, which saves time.
- [Indexing](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/indexing/) - Indexing builds data structures on table columns so searches and filters run faster. The cost is extra storage plus added overhead every time data is written.
- [Inference](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/inference/) - Inference is running a trained machine learning model on new, unseen data to produce predictions, classifications, or generated content. It follows training.
- [Internet of Things (IoT) Data](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/internet-of-things-iot-data/) - IoT data is the continuous stream of sensor readings, telemetry, and status updates produced by physical devices that are connected to the internet.
- [IVF-FLAT](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/ivf-flat/) - IVF-Flat is an inverted file index for vector databases that groups vectors into clusters and searches only those whose centroids are nearest the query vector.
- [JSON (JavaScript Object Notation)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/json-javascript-object-notation/) - JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a lightweight, text-based format for exchanging data. People can read and write it easily, and machines parse it quickly.
- [JSON-LD](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/json-ld/) - A method of encoding Linked Data using JSON, widely utilized to embed structured metadata schemas into website pages for search engine optimization.
- [K-Means Clustering](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/k-means-clustering/) - K-means is an unsupervised clustering algorithm that splits data into K distinct clusters by assigning each point to its nearest centroid by Euclidean distance.
- [K-Nearest Neighbors](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/k-nearest-neighbors/) - K-nearest neighbors (KNN) is a non-parametric algorithm for classification and regression that labels a point by a vote or average of its closest neighbors.
- [Kafka (Apache Kafka)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/kafka-apache-kafka/) - Apache Kafka is an open-source distributed event streaming platform used by thousands of companies for high-performance data pipelines and streaming analytics.
- [Kafka Connect](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/kafka-connect/) - Kafka Connect is the Apache Kafka component designed to simplify integration between Kafka topics and external data sources such as databases.
- [Key-Value Store](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/key-value-store/) - A key-value store is a simple NoSQL database built on an associative array (a map), storing data as a collection of unique keys each linked to a value.
- [KPI (Key Performance Indicator)](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/kpi-key-performance-indicator/) - A key performance indicator (KPI) is a quantifiable measure used to evaluate how well an organization, employee, or project is meeting its objectives.
- [Kubernetes](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/kubernetes/) - Kubernetes is an open-source container orchestration system that automates deploying, scaling, and managing containerized apps across clusters of machines.
- [Lakehouse Catalog](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/lakehouse-catalog/) - The metadata catalog interface that tracks transactional table namespaces and physical files in a data lakehouse, coordinating safe concurrent engine access.
- [Lakehouse Storage](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/lakehouse-storage/) - Lakehouse storage is the open cloud object storage layer holding transactional Parquet or ORC tables that are managed by table formats like Apache Iceberg.
- [LangChain](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/langchain/) - LangChain is an open-source framework for building applications on large language models, offering integrations, prompt templates, and chains of calls.
- [Large Language Model](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/large-language-model/) - A large language model (LLM) is an AI model trained on massive text datasets to understand, generate, translate, and summarize human language across many tasks.
- [Latent Space](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/latent-space/) - Latent space is a compressed mathematical space where similar data points sit closer together, capturing hidden features of the original input data.
- [Linear Regression](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/linear-regression/) - Linear regression is a basic supervised learning algorithm that models the relationship between dependent and independent variables by fitting a straight line.
- [Llama](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/llama/) - Llama is a family of open-source foundation large language models from Meta, widely used for running LLMs locally and as a base for custom fine-tuning projects.
- [LlamaIndex](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/llamaindex/) - A data framework for connecting private custom data sources to large language models, facilitating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and semantic indexing.
- [LLM Prompting](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/llm-prompting/) - LLM prompting is the practice of sending context-rich instruction templates to large language models in order to shape the output that they generate.
- [Load Balancer](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/load-balancer/) - A load balancer is a networking device or software that spreads incoming traffic across a group of backend servers to balance resource use and prevent overload.
- [Logistic Regression](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/logistic-regression/) - Logistic regression is a classification algorithm that predicts the probability of a binary outcome, such as yes or no, from a set of input features.
- [Loss Function](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/loss-function/) - A loss function measures the gap between a model's predictions and the actual target values during training, and that number guides model optimization.
- [Machine Learning](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/machine-learning/) - A branch of artificial intelligence focused on building systems that learn from data, identify patterns, and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
- [Manifest File](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/manifest-file/) - In Apache Iceberg, a manifest file is an Avro file listing data or delete files with partition-level metrics, so engines can prune files at query planning.
- [Manifest List](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/manifest-list/) - In Apache Iceberg, a manifest list is an Avro file that tracks a snapshot's manifest files and their partition specs, enabling partition-level metadata pruning.
- [Materialized View](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/materialized-view/) - A materialized view stores a query's precomputed results physically on disk, so complex queries need not be re-evaluated. Several refresh strategies exist.
- [Materialized View Refresh](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/materialized-view-refresh/) - Materialized view refresh is the technique for keeping precalculated views in sync with incoming transactional writes so their stored results stay current.
- [Merge-on-Read](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/merge-on-read/) - Merge-on-read is a write strategy that records updates and deletes in separate delete files, then merges them with the base data files when the data is read.
- [Monte Carlo](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/monte-carlo/) - Monte Carlo is an enterprise data observability platform designed to track, alert, and resolve issues related to data quality and reliability.
- [Open Source Tools](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/open-source/) - The Open Source Tools section of the Data & AI Wiki indexes open engines, table formats, catalogs, and orchestrators, from Apache Spark to Iceberg and Airflow.
- [Project Nessie](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/project-nessie/) - Project Nessie is an open-source transactional catalog for Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake tables that adds Git-like branches, commits, merges, and tags.
- [Shawn Gordon](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/shawn-gordon/) - Shawn Gordon is a Senior Developer Advocate at Collate, the company behind OpenMetadata, and a Grammy-nominated musician known for his educational content.
- [Snowflake](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/snowflake/) - Snowflake is a fully managed cloud data warehouse on AWS, GCP, and Azure that separates storage, compute, and services, running queries on virtual warehouses.
- [Trino](https://dataaiwiki.com/wiki/trino/) - Trino, formerly PrestoSQL, is an open-source distributed SQL engine for low-latency ad-hoc analytics that queries data in place and joins across systems.
